decision.rationale: Maintain BUY medium conviction. Five considerations: (1) FIRST DAILY CLOSE ABOVE $65K SINCE JULY 15 — The $65,380.37 reference is the highest close since July 15's $65,048 reference and is the FIRST DAILY CLOSE ABOVE $65,000 SINCE JULY 15 (five sessions ago). This resolves the $65,000 ceiling that had rejected BTC six times across four sessions. The close above $65,000 is the single most important technical milestone of the session. Volume confirmation (158.40 BTC breakout candle = session-highest) differentiates this breakout from the prior intraday failures. (2) SESSION HIGH $65,798.99 EXCEEDS JULY 15 MONTHLY HIGH — Today's session high of $65,798.99 at 18:00 UTC is the HIGHEST LEVEL SINCE AT LEAST JULY 15 and exceeds the July 15 monthly high of $65,558. BTC has now traded into new post-correction territory, establishing the price structure for a continuation toward $66,000–$67,000. (3) STOP AT $63,181 HELD THROUGH A SCARY TEST — The morning session low of $63,763.92 gave the stop $582 of clearance — the closest it has been tested since July 17's $62,523 intraday breach. Despite the ascending-session-low structure being broken (lower low: $64,279 July 19 → $63,763 July 20), the structural framework stop has not been triggered in six consecutive sessions. A daily close below $63,181 would still trigger the stop. (4) CLARITY ACT DETERIORATION — SIGNIFICANT HEADWIND — The CLARITY Act's Polymarket odds fell to 32% today (record low since January 2026), down from ~50% (coin flip) as recently as July 12. Three Democratic senators (Murphy, Van Hollen, Merkley) formally opposed. The merged draft omits the ethics provision Democrats explicitly demanded. This materially reduces the probability of the primary near-term bull catalyst materializing in this legislative window. However, BTC's $843 session gain DESPITE worsening CLARITY Act odds suggests the market is partially decoupling from this binary dependency — the technical breakout above $65K is self-reinforcing via short-squeeze mechanics regardless of legislative outcome. (5) OIL AT $88 BRENT — APPROACHING MACRO RED LINE — Brent crude hit ~$88 (briefly $91) today, up from July 19's '$72+', as the Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted and the US-Iran ceasefire has collapsed (Day 9). The prior dossier identified $90–$100 Brent as the 'red line' for macro risk-off BTC impact. We are now within $2 Brent of that threshold. Diplomatic mediation proposals from international mediators (announced today) provide a slim de-escalation path but do not resolve the structural conflict. This remains the most elevated macro tail risk in the near term. NET: The $65K close and $65,799 session high are decisive technical positives. The CLARITY Act deterioration and oil spike are serious headwinds. Medium conviction balances both — the technical picture has improved significantly, but the macro and legislative risks prevent upgrading to high conviction.

extra.label: CLARITY ACT POLYMARKET ODDS FALL TO 32% — RECORD LOW; ETHICS DEADLOCK DEEPENS
extra.value: The CLARITY Act (DAMCA) faces its most acute legislative challenge yet. Polymarket now prices BTC's primary regulatory catalyst at just 32% probability of passing by year-end — the record low since the Polymarket market launched in January 2026. Key developments today: (1) Senate Democrats (Senators Chris Murphy, Chris Van Hollen, and Jeff Merkley) held a formal press conference formally opposing the bill; (2) The merged Senate draft (combining Banking and Agriculture Committee versions) was released omitting the ethics provision that Democrats have explicitly named as the price of their floor votes; (3) A high-level White House meeting was reported to be planned to resolve the ethics standoff, but no resolution announced; (4) Senate Majority Leader Thune has pledged a floor vote before approximately August 7 recess cutoff — the remaining window is approximately 2.5 weeks. BTC's +1.3% gain today DESPITE these worsening CLARITY Act odds is significant: the market appears to be partially decoupling from this binary dependency. The technical breakout above $65K is self-reinforcing via short-squeeze mechanics and may be pricing in ETF demand and general crypto momentum rather than CLARITY Act passage. This reduces the upside magnitude if CLARITY Act does pass (less of a surprise) but also limits the downside if it fails (market has already partially priced in failure).

extra.label: BIP-110 GOVERNANCE DISPUTE — SAYLOR PUBLISHES 110-POINT OPPOSITION ESSAY
extra.value: Bitcoin's BIP-110 proposal — which would temporarily restrict arbitrary non-monetary data storage on the blockchain (targeting Ordinals/inscription 'spam') — has ignited a significant community governance debate. Michael Saylor (Strategy/MicroStrategy) published a 110-point essay titled '110 Reasons BIP-110 Is a Bad Idea' on July 18-19, arguing the proposal: (a) inserts human judgment into Bitcoin's consensus rules; (b) creates a dangerous censorship precedent by restricting fee-paying transactions based on content; (c) the lowered 55% activation threshold (vs. the traditional 95%) raises the risk of a chain split; and (d) undermines Bitcoin's neutrality which is a core value proposition. Market context: miner signaling support for BIP-110 stands at just 1.3% as of July 13 — virtually no miner community adoption. BIP-110's voluntary signaling deadline is expected at block 961,542 (approximately August 2026). While BIP-110 is extremely unlikely to activate at 1.3% miner support, Saylor's public opposition and chain-split warning add a governance uncertainty cloud to BTC's narrative just as it attempts a technical breakout. This is a medium-term secondary risk, not an immediate price driver, but the public debate draws attention to the Bitcoin community's internal tensions.

what_traders_are_doing: JULY 20 POST-CLOSE — FIRST $65K CLOSE IN FIVE SESSIONS ON VOLUME-CONFIRMED BREAKOUT; BULLISH REVERSAL DESPITE WORSENING CLARITY ACT ODDS AND OIL SPIKE TO BRENT $88. (1) THE TECHNICAL PICTURE — WHAT THE CANDLES SAY — Session highs: Jul 16 $64,997 → Jul 17 $64,392 → Jul 18 $64,744 → Jul 19 $64,971 → Jul 20 $65,798.99 (+$827 above prior high; new post-July 15 peak). Session lows: Jul 17 $62,523 → Jul 18 $63,886 → Jul 19 $64,279 → Jul 20 $63,763.92 (LOWER LOW — ascending structure broken). Reference closes: Jul 17 $64,115 → Jul 18 $64,700 → Jul 19 $64,537 → Jul 20 $65,380.37 (FIRST CLOSE ABOVE $65K). The picture in one sentence: bulls won on the close, but the morning low broke the ascending floor. This is a mixed-signal session where the close matters more than the low because the close above $65K is a structural milestone, while the $63,763 low is an intraday wick that was fully recaptured. (2) THE BREAKOUT — WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE MORNING DIP — The $65,000 level was tested and rejected on four prior sessions (six total failed approaches today before the 15:00 UTC candle succeeded). A level that has been tested multiple times and finally breaks tends to generate strong momentum because: (a) every bearish bet placed at $65,000 in those prior sessions was wrong and must be covered; (b) every long position that was stopped out above the $65,000 range during earlier rejections is now back in profit; (c) algorithmic breakout strategies trigger above $65,000 and above $65,200 (prior resistance bands); (d) media coverage of '$65K break' generates FOMO retail buying on Tuesday open. The 15:00 UTC candle was not just a price move — it was a mechanical squeeze of multiple overlapping bearish positions. (3) WHAT THE CLARITY ACT DETERIORATION MEANS — Polymarket at 32% changes the narrative. The July 19 dossier framed the CLARITY Act as the 'only identified catalyst with the magnitude to break $65,000.' But $65,000 was broken today WITHOUT the CLARITY Act clearing any hurdle.
